scope: SKT's official 4-bit checkpoint skt/A.X-K2-NVFP4 (full 61 layers) served on ONE Standard_ND96amsr_A100_v4 node (8 x A100-SXM4-80GB, Azure ML low priority), tensor parallel 8, native DSA, one OpenAI-compatible endpoint; compared with the FP8 checkpoint on two nodes (16 x A100, TP8 x PP2) and with the tech report's Fig. 7 (FP8 on one 8 x B200 node).

checkpoint.quantization: ModelOpt MIXED_PRECISION (producer modelopt 0.44.0-axk2-mixed-fp8-nvfp4experts), from hf_quant_config.json: the routed experts of the 60 MoE layers (256 experts x gate/up/down = 46,080 linears) NVFP4 with group size 16; attention including the DSA indexer (wq_b, wk), the shared experts and layer 0's dense MLP FP8; excluded (BF16): lm_head, embed_tokens, norms and the MoE router (*.mlp.gate); no KV-cache quantization
checkpoint.skt_documented_setup: 4 x B200, TP4 + expert parallel, FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE, VLLM_USE_FLASHINFER_MOE_FP4=1
checkpoint.skt_model_card_claims: routed experts NVFP4 W4A4; 'retains performance comparable to the FP8 checkpoint while reducing the model memory footprint by approximately half'; NIAH 100 at every length and depth to 512K (YaRN) after NVFP4 quantization. Not re-measured here beyond the needle test below.

engine_change.why: vLLM 0.23 (and SKT's fork) refuses this checkpoint below compute capability 8.9: ModelOptMixedPrecisionConfig.get_min_capability() returns 89. Upstream vLLM lowered it to 80 because both halves already have SM80 paths: NVFP4 experts through Marlin W4A16 and FP8 layers through Marlin W8A16.

upstream_prs.title: [Kernel] Consolidate Marlin thread-tile padding across all dense Marlin paths
upstream_prs.taken: only its modelopt.py line: ModelOptFp8LinearMethod.create_weights sets layer.orig_dtype, which prepare_fp8_layer_for_marlin reads. The tile-padding part is not needed because every A.X-K2 per-rank GEMM shape at TP8 is already Marlin-aligned (N % 64 == 0, K % 128 == 0).

engine_change.applied_on: SKT-AI/vllm axk2-v0.23.0 @ 023bc76025459d6356c5885f271b9b95c50f93b6 (its modelopt.py is byte-identical to upstream v0.23.0)

log_notes: vLLM logs 'Detected ModelOpt NVFP4 checkpoint' twice, once with quant_algo=NVFP4 and once with quant_algo=W4A16_NVFP4. ModelOptMixedPrecisionConfig always builds a sibling W4A16_NVFP4 config for layers that declare that algorithm (vllm v0.23.0 modelopt.py:2281-2300). This checkpoint's routed experts declare NVFP4; on SM80 the NVFP4 MoE method selects the MARLIN backend, which runs them weight-only (FP4 weights, BF16 activations), as the 'does not have native support for FP4 computation' line states.

With 8,192 batched tokens the KV cache got 18.53 GiB per GPU (254,016 tokens), so --max-model-len -1 auto-fitted the context to 254,016. With 2,048 batched tokens the activation reserve is smaller: 19.91 GiB, 272,960 tokens, and the full 262,144-token context fits.
Weights take 48.5 GiB per GPU on 8 GPUs (FP8 checkpoint: 41.7 GiB per GPU on 16 GPUs). Peak GPU memory was 77,411 MiB on every GPU (gpu_memory_utilization 0.92).
interpretation: Decode at low and moderate concurrency is bound by reading weights. NVFP4 halves the bytes of the routed experts, which dominate a decode step, so 8 A100s decode as fast as 16 A100s with the FP8 checkpoint: one request at 1K input runs at 19.0 ms per output token against 19.2 ms, and concurrency 8-32 at 1.01-1.06x the output tok/s (matched comparison, 2,048 batched tokens on both sides).
With more requests in flight the step becomes compute- and attention-heavy and half the GPUs show: 0.86x at concurrency 64 and 0.81x at 128.

Prefill is compute-bound. A100 has no FP4 or FP8 tensor cores, so prefill runs BF16 math with either checkpoint, on half as many GPUs here: one 32K-token prompt takes 11.6 s to the first token against 7.2 s.

The BF16 MLA KV cache is replicated on every tensor-parallel rank. One node holds 254,016 tokens (8,192 batched tokens) against 673,792 on the two FP8 nodes, so under the tech report's Fig. 7 conditions 15 of 32 requests ran at 16K inputs and 7 at 32K.

Against Fig. 7 (FP8 on one 8 x B200 node) the 8 A100s reach 0.47-0.49x at 1K-4K inputs, about twice the per-GPU throughput of the FP8 checkpoint on 16 A100s (0.21-0.24x per GPU), and 0.20-0.35x at 8K-32K, where the KV cache and prefill limit them.

The rest of the gap is hardware: B200 has 3.9x the memory bandwidth (8 vs 2.0 TB/s) and FP8/FP4 tensor cores (4,500/9,000 dense TFLOPS against A100's 312 BF16), and on B200 SKT runs the NVFP4 experts W4A4.
Cost per million output tokens falls by 56% at concurrency 32 (1K in, 1K out) and by about 40% at concurrency 128 (1K in, 256 out) at every price meter, because one node replaces two.

Two NVFP4 replicas on the two nodes that the FP8 deployment uses, behind one load balancer, would give about twice the short-input throughput of that deployment and two independent KV caches. This is an estimate from the one-node numbers, not a measurement.

Quality was checked only with the functional probes (4/4), tool calls (9/9) and SKT's needle test (9/9 up to 244,898 prompt tokens). SKT reports NVFP4 quality comparable to FP8; benchmark parity on A100 was not measured.
